text: Lisinopril is a competitive inhibitor of Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme (ACE) and does not function as a direct pharmacological ligand for the ERBB2 (HER2) receptor. While some studies suggest that ACE inhibitors may indirectly modulate the tumor microenvironment or interfere with HER2-driven signaling pathways via crosstalk with the EGFR/HER2 axis, there is no established direct binding affinity or molecular docking mechanism between lisinopril and the ERBB2 protein. Consequently, lisinopril is not a therapeutic agent for HER2-positive breast cancer, and its clinical use in this context remains limited to managing hypertension in patients undergoing cardiotoxic chemotherapy (e.g., trastuzumab).
